title: Human-first room conversation: human-only posts, member replies in shared threads, and a thread side panel in one contextual right pane
summary: Add a Control-authorized Space append that stores a human post or thread reply in Session Core without starting a model turn, let any member holding that decision reply in any room thread (Session Core still applies an owner-only check to Space threads), keep thread counters at write time, and record a per-thread agent-engagement fact so an agent that has spoken in a thread hears follow-ups. Render threads in a generalised right-hand AuxPane (standard header, resize, focus hand-off) bound to ?thread=, so the thread deep links that Activity already emits finally open the thread.
whyItMatters: Every room post is a model invocation today, and non-owners cannot reply although the UI offers Reply. Until people can talk to each other in shared threads, a Space is a shared AI prompt box rather than a Teams or Slack room. Mentions, notifications, search, reactions and edits all attach to these entries, and the AuxPane is the host for runs, members and agent sessions later.

title: Addressed agent wake-up: several agents per message, per-binding respond_to/subscribe trigger policy, offer-to-add, then optional ambient participation
summary: Stop treating every room post as a model turn. Add a human-only post path, then let a message wake an agent only when it is addressed (one or several agents, with an address lock in the composer) or matches a binding trigger rule, with per-binding respond_to (owner|allowlist|anyone|nobody) and subscribe (mentions|all|rules) fields and an offer-to-add dialog for an unbound agent. Later add an optional cheap ambient judge with standing orders and an auditable ledger, and a room tool so an agent may stay silent.
whyItMatters: A Space is meant to feel like Slack/Teams for people first, with agents joining on demand. Today the composer sends every post through the chat stream, so people cannot simply talk to each other and an agent cannot be silent. This is the single change that makes a Space a room instead of a chat with a bot, and every other agent feature (cards, multi-agent, personal agents) builds on addressed-only wake-up.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Buzz binding fields respond_to owner|allowlist|anyone|nobody (fails closed) and subscribe mentions|all|rules; rules are first-match-wins over (content, author, kind, channel) with a timeout and length cap; the composer keeps a persistent per-composer set of addressed agents and records implicit mentions as provenance so edits can strip them; unaddressed messages reach agents only as overheard context. Mention of an agent the author owns but the room lacks opens an Invite+send vs send-as-reference dialog with a fresh authorization per destination; wake publishes the message first, then starts the agent with a replay floor. QM ambient: per-room cursor, a cheap judge prompt (identity + standing orders + do-not-act backdrop + new batch) returns {act, reason, asked_by}; every judgment is stored for admins; ChannelPolicy {orders, bots: ignore|rollup|action|user, ambientEnabled} edited with compare-and-swap and history. QM room tool: post/reach/react/edit/read_thread actions where post rejects destination arguments and a turn that ends without a post is silent.

title: Space realtime substrate: typed seq-numbered event projection, resumable per-Space SSE through the gateway, and authorization at subscribe and at every delivery
summary: Have the Application Plane emit one typed, metadata-only Space event envelope with a per-Space monotonic seq (reusing the leased Convex outbox pattern already used for lifecycle events), let the gateway terminate one resumable SSE per tab (Last-Event-ID, cursor_too_old snapshot frame, heartbeats under 15 s, a watchdog, the 6 s poll kept as fallback), and send every frame through one fail-closed chokepoint that holds a live Control read decision for (user, Space, audience revision) and closes the stream on revocation or audience change.
whyItMatters: All five references push room events; Verevon polls the full thread list every 6 s, so other members see posts and agent replies late, and every live feature (shared run streams, unread counts, presence, calls) has nothing to ride on. Checking authority at subscribe and at every delivery keeps the push tier from becoming a side door around Control decisions and ZDR.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-09-01] Client opens one stream after auth and sends per-room cursors {room, generation, after_seq}. Server replies connected{stream_id, server_time}, replays rows with seq > after_seq from a bounded window (or sends cursor_too_old so the client re-snapshots), then live frames (rows, deletes, ephemeral presence/typing, agent state, roster change, heartbeat). Client opens live first then backfills and dedupes by id; resume is triggered by online/focus/visibilitychange events (min 5 s apart), never by writing to a half-open socket from a watchdog. On silence the client falls back to polling with jittered reconnect, and while healthy it polls at a relaxed 60-180 s to heal silent drift. [R-t1-09-03] Envelope {id, room_id, seq, kind, author, created_at, refs, body_ref}; append-only; consumers dispatch on kind and ignore unknown kinds; derived state (membership, reply counts, presence snapshots) is emitted as server-authored projection events; a generation bump invalidates replicas. Bus topics {tenant}:room:{id}; a node subscribes only while it has local subscribers (refcount, delayed unsubscribe about 500 ms) and forces client resync after a bus reconnect because messages in the gap are lost. [R-t1-09-02] Subscription registry indexed by (room, kind). On every outbound event: tenant label equality, per-kind audience rules, room membership from a 10 s cache, fail closed on lookup error. On subscribe: load accessible rooms, apply the token scope upper bound, repair negative cache entries against the database, then register. On revocation: publish an idempotent cache-invalidate hint (loss tolerable) and a separate connection-control command that closes affected sockets on every node, so hints and kill commands are never conflated.

title: Space notifications: typed signals for mentions, replies, approvals and agent completions, refs-only payload, rate limits, per-room levels and thread follow/mute
summary: Let conversation-core, capability-core and Control publish typed signals (mention, reply, approval_needed, agent_done, agent_awaiting, invite) into notification-core through a per-service, per-type producer allowlist, with one shared refs-only payload (signal, space, thread, message or run ref, actor, urgency, actions, trace id, deep link) and a rate limit. Add per-room levels (All, Mentions, Off), a hide-preview flag that defaults on for ZDR orgs, and per-user thread follow/mute with auto-follow reasons, applying a fixed rule order (a mention passes, then mute, then thread rules).
whyItMatters: No Space event produces a notification today: the producer allowlist only admits run_completed and run_failed, and mention.received is seeded but never produced. People will not notice a mention or an agent waiting on them, which undercuts both the Teams/Slack and the agent half of the vision.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-05-01] Slack validates one schema-checked payload (team, channel, message and thread ids plus a trace id) and runs it through display-allowed and DND gates, with telemetry for received, click, reply and action. Grok Bot's agent-turn notification carries agent id, message preview, last message id and an awaiting_user_response flag, so 'done' and 'needs you' are different signals. Teams keeps the signal enum closed (call, mention, chat, channel, other) so routing rules stay manageable. Grok Bot throttles at a minimum interval of 5000 ms and 10 per 300 s window and only notifies the active device. Buzz default: rooms silent (mentions still pass), DMs urgent-only, workflow and approval on, agent chatter off. Buzz lesson: it declared agent job kinds but never emitted them, leaving dead settings rows, so declare only signals that have a producer. [R-t1-05-04] Slack: a global level with per-conversation exceptions, separate desktop and mobile settings and a no-text-in-notifications flag mirrored into the native layer. Teams: auto-follow when mentioned, when my message gets a reply and when I reply, plus a 'replies to followed threads' setting. Buzz decision function: mention always passes, then channel mute, then thread rules (participated, followed, authored, muted roots), then slot enabled, then an alert-while-viewing check; mutes, stars and sections live in one per-user replaceable state with last-writer-wins merge across devices.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: [R-t1-05-01] The producer allowlist (isNotificationTypeAuthorized) lets verevon-gateway send only notification.created to the delegated user itself, support-worker its ticket and SLA types, and capability-core only modelplane.run_completed and modelplane.run_failed. mention.received is seeded in channel config but has no producer. @person mentions are inserted as plain text with no server record. There is no signal taxonomy and no deep-link contract for Space or thread. The per-user run watcher ('notify me when this run finishes') is the only Space-adjacent producer. [R-t1-05-04] notification-core has per-event by per-channel preferences and the gateway proxies them, but there is no per-room level, no hide-preview flag, no desktop and mobile split and no UI in Spaces. A grep of verevonv3 src/features found no thread follow or mute (INF); the Space definition names pause and mute only for an agent's presence in a room, not for notifications.

approachOriginal: [R-t1-05-01] conversation-core: persist a mention record on post (refs only, no body) and emit mention and reply events. capability-core: extend beyond run_completed and run_failed to agent_done, agent_awaiting and approval_needed. Control: emit invite. notification-core: extend isNotificationTypeAuthorized per service and signal, add the Space signal types, and define the payload as a shared contract; the body is refs-only for ZDR orgs and a preview is included only when retention mode allows (check at enqueue, matching the worker's existing refusal of async ZDR delivery). Deep link as a stable route (web path plus a verevon:// form) carrying space, thread and message ids plus the trace id. Seed defaults in notification-core config: mentions, approvals and agent-awaiting-you on; room posts and agent progress off; per-room override comes in this item (R-t1-05-04). Add a per-recipient and per-agent-sender token bucket in the router. The device-routing half of the cross-device cluster (active-device suppression) ships with push in F-t1-035 (R-t1-05-05). title: Cross-room attention: a server-side unread/working aggregate stream, then a Home 'needs you' inbox with Agents and Activity destinations
summary: Keep a per-Space latest-activity aggregate (last seq, author kind, run state) in the Application Plane, join it with the durable per-member read markers into a per-user {unread, mentions, needs_you} map pushed over the realtime stream (mark-all-read, defined badge semantics, presence and typing as ephemeral leases on the same path). referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-05-03] Teams materialises about 60 typed activity kinds and exposes slices (Mentions, Threads, Tag mentions, VIP, Reminders, Drafts, Saved, Requests) as saved filters with show rules. Grok Bot unifies approvals, NEEDS_INPUT tasks, hand-off requests and routine failures into one queue with a reason and dismissable trays. QM pushes {threadRef, state, participants} over one SSE stream with stale-delta rejection and refetch on resync. Buzz also collapses notes from one agent within 5 minutes into a single card; borrow that grouping rule for the Agents slice. [R-t1-05-02] Server keeps a per-member read marker per room (and per followed thread) and a per-room latest-activity aggregate. Unread equals latest activity later than last read, for rooms the user has not muted, counted only for event kinds allowed to badge. [R-t1-12-02] File-based routes per destination; a pinned header component holds search plus fixed feature entries, below it fixed conversation groups plus user sections; a narrow rail switches tenants. Teams models the app bar as {appId, pinned, order} with a keyboard drag state machine (pickup, move, place/cancel) announced through a live region. Build as a <Rail> of route entries from a typed destinations registry, checked for permission the way QM does.
